title: fix: request reasoning summaries from Azure Responses API
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- body.reasoning previously set only effort, so Azure Responses did not generate reasoning-summary text even though the model produced billed reasoning tokens.
- Adds summary: auto to the reasoning request field so the existing streaming and non-streaming relay can expose the summary as reasoning_content.
- Current Microsoft Azure documentation supports auto for GPT-5 reasoning summaries. GPT-5 models do not support concise, so auto is intentional and no fallback is needed.
- Enabling summaries can add output tokens and latency for callers that explicitly set reasoning_effort.

## Validation

- npx vitest run test/text/azureResponsesClient.test.ts — 12/12 passed
- npm run typecheck — passed
- npx biome check on both changed files — passed
- GitHub checks — passed

gist.headline: The thoughts come through
gist.blurb: Azure GPT-5 was doing the thinking but keeping its notes to itself. Now callers who ask for reasoning effort can receive the reasoning summary too.
gist.summary: Azure Responses requests now send `reasoning.summary: "auto"` alongside `reasoning.effort`, allowing GPT-5 reasoning summaries to reach Pollinations streaming and non-streaming clients as `reasoning_content`.
gist.impact: Callers that explicitly set `reasoning_effort` can now receive Azure GPT-5's generated reasoning summary instead of only being billed for unseen reasoning tokens.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Azure GPT-5 reasoning as a friendly pastel cloud-terminal producing a neatly unrolled thought-summary scroll, rather than hiding it inside the machine. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, catches and reads the glowing scroll beside a retro terminal, with code-plants and flowers showing that the hidden reasoning has become useful visible output.
